strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses genuine inflexibility in current safety monitoring approaches with clear motivation for dynamic guardrails
Novel progressive training scheme: clever sequential term training that ensures nested subclassifiers perform well; recovers linear probes exactly at truncation 1
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 4 LLMs × 2 datasets × 16 layers with parameter-matched baselines, thorough ablations (rank, degree, training scheme), and multiple random seeds
Consistent improvements across conditions: TPCs match or exceed baselines in essentially all settings, demonstrating robustness across models and datasets
Two complementary evaluation modes: safety dial (compute-accuracy tradeoff) and adaptive cascade (input-dependent compute) are well-motivated and practical
Better interpretability than MLPs: explicit attribution to neuron pair interactions provides transparency advantage over black-box alternatives
Strong reproducibility: code promised, extensive implementation details, clear hyperparameter documentation, and rigorous experimental methodology
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: polynomial classifiers and symmetric CP factorization are established techniques; main contribution is in combination and application rather than fundamental innovations
Modest performance improvements: typical gains of 1-2% over linear probes and 1-6% over MLPs; larger improvements (10%) only for specific sub-categories, limiting practical impact

Interpretability advantage overstated: authors acknowledge feature combinations are 'dense and lack obvious legibility to humans'; effect magnitudes tiny (±0.001-0.005) with only one example shown and no quantitative evaluation
Limited mechanistic insight: paper doesn't explain why polynomials help or when they're necessary; missing analysis of which harm categories benefit and why
Mean pooling over tokens unjustified: significant design simplification that loses positional/sequential information with no ablation or comparison to alternatives

Small batch size performance: Figure 12 shows TPCs substantially slower than EE-MLPs at batch sizes 1-1024, which are realistic for per-request monitoring; claimed 'medium/large batch' advantage may not hold in practice
Cascading defense under-explored: threshold τ selection appears ad-hoc; limited sensitivity analysis; computational cost (Section D) theoretical; no principled guidance for practitioners

Limited evaluation scope: only binary prompt-level classification on two similar datasets; no output monitoring, no comparison to LLM-as-judge baselines (most practically relevant), unclear generalization
Hyperparameter selection unclear: R=64 and N=5 somewhat arbitrary; no principled method for practitioners to choose these without extensive ablations
Small data regime unaddressed: authors acknowledge not exploring performance with limited labels, a common constraint in safety applications

strengths: Clear practical motivation: Dynamic safety monitoring addresses a real problem of efficiently deploying safety guardrails; the two evaluation modes (safety dial and adaptive cascade) are genuinely useful

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 4 LLMs (3B-30B), 2 datasets, 16 layers, extensive ablations, parameter-matched baselines, cross-dataset evaluation, well-calibrated models, and multiple random seeds
Novel progressive training scheme: Section 3.2.1 properly formulates a training approach that ensures truncated models perform well, addressing a gap in prior polynomial classifier work
Interpretability advantages: Built-in neuron interaction attribution provides genuine advantages over black-box MLPs, important for safety-critical applications
Technical soundness: Symmetric CP decomposition is well-motivated; cascading with confidence thresholds is sensible; reproducibility is strong with promised code and detailed hyperparameters
Clear presentation: Well-structured with effective figures and accessible explanations of core ideas
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Polynomial classifiers and CP decomposition are established. The main contribution—truncated progressive evaluation—is a relatively straightforward extension. The technical depth is incremental for a top venue

Mixed empirical results across datasets: TPCs underperform EE-MLPs on BeaverTails test set in 3/4 models (Table 1b); improvements on WildGuardMix are often modest (1-3%). Paper compensates by citing validation set performance, weakening the claims

Non-monotonic performance with increasing compute: Section 5 acknowledges that both TPCs and MLPs 'often fail to yield monotonically increasing performance with additional test-time compute'—fundamentally undermining the central claim of scaling safety with compute

Cascading evaluation lacks rigor: Confidence threshold τ is a hyperparameter without principled selection guidance; fairness of comparisons between cascaded and fixed-order evaluation is unclear; relationship to uncertainty quantification is unexplored

Limited analysis of when/why TPCs work: No investigation of task characteristics determining polynomial effectiveness; why higher-order terms help in some subcategories (10%) but not others is unexplained; polynomial degree N=5 is somewhat arbitrary

Practical deployment concerns: At small batch sizes (realistic for always-on monitoring), EE-MLPs are faster (Fig. 13); mean pooling over tokens loses positional information; layer selection remains a required hyperparameter
Cross-dataset generalization weaknesses: Very low precision on ToxicChat/OpenAI-Moderation due to differing harm labeling standards (Section F.2), raising broader robustness concerns beyond TPCs
Incomplete comparison to related work: No direct evaluation of two-stage cascades from McKenzie et al. (2025) and Cunningham et al. (2025), which are the most relevant baselines for this problem

Feature attribution limited practical utility: Section 4.4's neuron interaction visualization is dense; authors acknowledge feature combinations 'lack obvious legibility to humans,' with unclear practical value for practitioners

Missing statistical rigor: No significance testing of improvements across random seeds despite often modest differences between methods; progressive training justification lacks ablations comparing to joint training
